asked_by: Madhav, 26 Oct 2026 (India chat): "evaluate rupee versus dollar, evaluate against stock prices so that to see how it is influencing"
title: Rupee against the dollar: does a sharply weaker rupee precede weaker Indian stocks (and stronger exporters)?
hypothesis: After a sharp weakening of the rupee (USD/INR up) the Nifty and Bank Nifty do worse over the next 5 and 20 sessions, while the exporters (Nifty IT, Nifty Pharma) do better than the Nifty; and TWT-H42 restated on the rupee: when USD/INR is up 5%+ over 126 sessions, or breaks above its 3-year high, the Nifty's next 21 and 63 sessions are weaker.

data.usdinr: FRED DEXINUS (Federal Reserve H.10, rupees per US dollar, New York noon buying rate), already in silver/macro/macro.parquet from 1990 (fetched by the macro job; US data, not an Indian market file, so it is not split into the sealed tree); research reads rows before 2024 only
data.index: silver/kite_index/day (NIFTY 50, NIFTY BANK, NIFTY IT, NIFTY PHARMA) 2003-2023

timing: a DEXINUS value dated d (a New York rate) is used from the Indian session after d (merge on d <= session date - 1 day, as india.teachers_stock.market_context does for US data); index outcomes run from the next session's close

definitions.dep5: USD/INR change over the last 5 FRED observations
definitions.weak5: dep5 in the top decile of its own trailing 756-observation distribution (the threshold uses only data known at the time)
definitions.weak1: the 1-observation change in the top decile of its trailing 756-observation distribution
definitions.h42_up5: USD/INR up 5% or more over 126 observations
definitions.h42_break3y: USD/INR above its highest value of the previous 756 observations

outcomes: nfwd5/nfwd20/nfwd21/nfwd63 = Nifty from the next close; bankfwd20 = Nifty Bank; itx20 / pharmax20 = Nifty IT / Nifty Pharma 20-session return minus the Nifty's over the same window
statistics: india.teachers_stock.msplit (market timing: quarter blocks of 'on' against 'off' sessions, Welch t); development 2003-2017, validation 2018-2023; india/registry.record standard rule, MIN_DATES 16

bar.note: a new family 'fx'; k frozen at the 10 variants below. The earlier context study C09 (usdinr_rising, family 'context') is related and its rows stay where they are

caveat_written_first: The rupee drifts weaker over the long run (about 3-4% a year), so 'breaks its 3-year high' is common; this is part of the claim as stated, not a flaw found afterwards.
not_claimed: No paper rule changes from this study.
